reasons: Lake identity lists case_name as Florida v. Wells, court as U.S. Supreme Court, date_decided as 1990-04-18, and year as 1990.
Lake citations list official cite 495 U.S. 1, parallel cites 110 S. Ct. 1632, 109 L. Ed. 2d 1, 58 U.S.L.W. 4454, and vendor neutral cite 1990 U.S. LEXIS 2035.
The opinion is an inventory-search case: the search was an inventory search of an impounded car and a locked suitcase.
The holding limits inventory searches by requiring standardized criteria or established routine to regulate opening containers, and by rejecting uncanalized discretion.
residual_risks: The word Key is partly editorial, but the SCOTUS source, citation count in the lake, and central closed-container inventory rule support the role.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: If desired, narrow the role note to closed-container inventory searches.

defect.evidence_quote: Our view that standardized criteria, ibid., or established routine, Illinois v. Lafayette, 462 U. S. 640, 648 (1983), must regulate the opening of containers found during inventory searches is based on the principle that an inventory search must not be a ruse for a general rummaging in order to discover incriminating evidence.
defect.problem: The holding field is truncated after 'standardized criteria or established…', leaving the core rule incomplete even though the intended proposition is supported by the opinion.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace with: An inventory search must not be a ruse for general rummaging to discover incriminating evidence; standardized criteria or an established routine must regulate the opening of containers found during inventory searches.

reasons: The opinion expressly supports the anti-rummaging principle and the standardized-criteria-or-established-routine requirement.
The current text is not wrong in direction, but it is incomplete as framed.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Complete the holding sentence and specify that the rule concerns opening containers found during inventory searches.

reasons: Lens A does not audit treatment or currency.

The asserted treatment fields match the disclosed lake treatment fields: field_i_validity good_law, as_of_content 1990-04-18, as_of_treatment 2026-06-30, composite_basis migration-seed, composite_basis_ref Florida v. Wells, and varies_by_point false.
residual_risks: Treatment correctness is reserved for Lens B.

reasons: Lake identity lists court_level as scotus and court as U.S. Supreme Court.
The authority-weight label Binding — SCOTUS follows from the disclosed court identity.
residual_risks: Treatment/currency analysis is outside Lens A.
